rationale: Abstract noun paired with ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ 'righteousness' as a judicial-moral quality. Lyc. ⲝ for ϫ; root possibly ϫⲡⲓⲟ ('reprove, censure'). Rendered 'judiciousness' to capture the corrective-evaluative sense. Confidence low pending parallels.
Qualitative adjective in two contexts (line 2: 'their wicked heart'; line 24: 'his other wicked associates'). Negative-moral sense from context; precise etymology unclear.
Verb paired with ⲍⲁⲧⲃⲟⲩ 'kill them' in a sequence of capital-punishment actions. Possibly Lyc. ⲡⲉϩⲧ-/ϩⲉⲧ- 'cast down, throw down.' Confidence low.

Used in compounds for the King of Darkness's confederates and the 'companions of Sin' (archons). Distinct from ⲡⲇⲟⲣⲙⲁ 'people' and from named power-classes. Possibly a Lyc. lexeme for 'comrade, fellow.' Confidence low.
Greek loanword τόλμα with Lyc. ⲇ for τ. In the context of judicial servants who 'do the will of their lord with might and reception and ⲇⲗⲁⲙ' the sense of 'firmness, boldness in execution' fits.
Likely Lyc. ⲥⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'side-of-back, behind.' Spatial adverb describing how the judged were bound — possibly facing-away from light. Confidence moderate.
Verb of judicial punishment occurring twice (lines 7 and 32) in disciplinary lists. Possibly related to ϣⲏⲧ 'punish, afflict' or ⲱϣⲧ̄ 'hang up.' Confidence low.
